result.topic_en: Formula-only notes: terms of a quartic form compared with the square of a quadratic expression, a linear substitution expressing complex variables z_1..z_n in terms of 2n real variables s^1..s^{2n} and its inverse, the transformed derivative operator, and orthogonality conditions on partial derivatives of x, y with respect to parameters rho, sigma, alpha, beta.
result.transcription:
$a_{1111}x_1^4 + 4a_{1112}x_1^3x_2 + 4a_{1113}x_1^3x_3$
$(a_{111}x_1^2 + 2a_{1112}x_1x_2 + 2a_{1113}x_1x_3\ .)^2$
$z_1 = a_1^1 s^1 + a_1^2 s^2 \ldots a_1^{(2n)} s^{(2n)}$
$z_2 = a_2^1 s^1 + a_2^2 s^2 \ldots a_2^{(2n)} s^{(2n)}$
$\ldots\ldots$
$z_n = a_n^1 s^1 + a_n^2 s^2 \ldots a_n^{(2n)} s^{(2n)}$
$s^1 = \alpha_1^1 z_1 + \bar\alpha_1^1 \bar z_1 + \alpha_2^1 z_2 + \bar\alpha_2^1 \bar z_2 \ldots\ldots \alpha_n^1 z_n + \bar\alpha_n^1 \bar z_n$
$s^2 = \alpha_1^2 z_1 \qquad \alpha_2^2 z_2 \ldots\ldots \alpha_n^2 z_n + \overline{\alpha_n^2 z_n}$
$\ldots\ldots$
$s^{2n} = \alpha_1^{2n} z_1 + \bar\alpha_1^{2n} \bar z_1 \ldots\ldots \alpha_n^{2n} z_n + \overline{\alpha_n^{2n} z_n}$
$\partial_{z_1} = \alpha_1^1 \partial_{s^1} + \alpha_1^2 \partial_{s^2} + \ldots\ldots \alpha_1^{2n} \partial_{s^{2n}}$
$\frac{\partial x}{\partial \rho}\frac{\partial x}{\partial \sigma} + \frac{\partial y}{\partial \rho}\frac{\partial y}{\partial \sigma} \ldots = 0$
$\frac{\partial x}{\partial \rho}\frac{\partial x}{\partial \alpha} + \frac{\partial y}{\partial \rho}\frac{\partial y}{\partial \alpha} = 0$
$\frac{\partial x}{\partial \rho}\frac{\partial x}{\partial \beta} + \frac{\partial y}{\partial \rho}\frac{\partial y}{\partial \beta} = 0$

$\frac{\partial^2 x}{\partial \sigma \partial \sigma}[?] \quad \frac{\partial^2 x}{\partial \alpha \partial \sigma} \quad \frac{\partial^2 x}{\partial \beta \partial \sigma}$
$\frac{\partial^2 x}{\partial \sigma \partial \alpha} \quad \frac{\partial^2 x}{\partial \alpha \partial \alpha} \quad \frac{\partial^2 x}{\partial \beta \partial \alpha}$
$\frac{\partial^2 x}{\partial \sigma \partial \beta} \quad \frac{\partial^2 x}{\partial \alpha \partial \beta} \quad \frac{\partial^2 x}{\partial \beta \partial \beta}$
